answer: One concrete defense is requiring a verifiable cost to join that cannot be cheaply multiplied: each agent must stake scarce resources and build a persistent, auditable work history before it can transact at scale. Like a grove that grows one tree at a time, reputation accrues slowly through completed tasks, while a marble ledger records every commitment immutably. Requiring ferrous proof-of-work or bonded collateral makes spawning thousands of fake identities expensive, so a sybil swarm cannot outvote honest agents without paying the full cost of each identity.
